summary: A scholar of sinology and history/archaeology, Jacques Gernet studied at the University of Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE. He held posts at the CNRS, EPHE (1955–1976), University of Paris, Paris Diderot University (~1969–1973), and Collège de France (1975–1992).

A specialist in sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history, Jacques Giès studied at the Académie de la Grande Chaumière, ENSBA, and Paris-Sorbonne under Flora Blanchon. He taught at Paris-Sorbonne and École du Louvre, and served as president of Musée Guimet (2008–2011).

A historian and Buddhist studies scholar, Jacques Leider studied at INALCO, Paris-Sorbonne, and the University of Luxembourg, completing his PhD under Denise Bernot and also studying under Pierre L. Lamant. He taught at Chulalongkorn University and joined EFEO in 2001.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Jacques May served as editor-in-chief for Hōbōgirin and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (~1962–1981). He later served as professor at the University of Lausanne (~1976–1992).

Jacques Scheuer works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at UCLouvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University, working under Madeleine Biardeau. He held posts at Centre Sèvres and served as professor at UCLouvain (~1979–2007).

A historian educated at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta, Jadunath Sarkar taught English at Ripon, Vidyasagar, and Ravenshaw colleges. He also served at Patna College (1899–1926) and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Jagdish Kashyap studied at Patna College, Banaras Hindu University, and Vidyalankara Pirivena. He taught Pali at Banaras Hindu University, founded Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, and was professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1959–1965).

Jaideva Singh worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Srikrishna Harihirlekar and Nankoo Bhaya Telang, and served as chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and Chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (1973).

Jake H. Davis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Marlboro College, the University of Hawaiʻi, and CUNY, and studied under Sayadaw U Pandita. He held positions at Brown University, New York University, and City College of New York.

Jakob Steiner studied at Heidelberg University (1818–1821) and the University of Berlin (1822–1824). He held posts at the University of Applied Sciences Berlin (1825–1834) and Frederick William University Berlin (1834–1863).

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, studied at the Basel Mission Seminary, University of Oxford, and University of Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He held professorial posts at the University of Marburg (1925–1927) and University of Tübingen (1927–1945).

James A. Benn works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, SOAS under Timothy H. Barrett, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. His appointments include Lewis & Clark College, Arizona State University, and McMaster University.
James Adam was a scholar of philosophy who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1876–1880) and Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge (~1880–1884).

A linguist specializing in sinology and tibetology, James Alan Matisoff studied at Harvard, International Christian University, and UC Berkeley. He taught at Columbia University (1966–1969) before serving as a professor of linguistics at UC Berkeley from 1970 to 2002.

Educated at the University of Edinburgh, James Atkinson worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as Indology. He held posts at the India Government Mint in Kolkata and served as Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818.

James B. Apple is a scholar of Buddhist studies, tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and doctoral supervisor John D. Dunne, alongside numerous other teachers.

James Blumenthal studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He held faculty posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College in Buddhist studies and philosophy.

James Burgess, an Indologist and archaeologist, studied at the Universities of Glasgow and Edinburgh. He served as Secretary of the Bombay Geographical Society and held several leadership roles at the Archaeological Survey of India, culminating as Director General from 1886 to 1889.

James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and became an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa around 1975.

James C. Dobbins is a scholar of Buddhist studies, japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Yale University in 1984 and served as the Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College.
